The route is 'climb any of the heathery gullies at the north or northeast head of the cirque' — the row itself records that there is no established line and no fixed gear anywhere in the cirque, and that two parties can be on quite different terrain a few metres apart. Independent searching returned the grade and nothing else. A baseFinding here could only say 'you are in the cirque', which does not answer how you know you have arrived at the start of the climbing. The cirque IS named as a negative test inside the Northwest Ridge and West Ridge entries — if you are on heather rather than rock, and you crossed no schrund, you are in it.
_SKIPPED.wa_eldorado_peak_northeast_face: POSITIONED ONLY RELATIVE TO THE EAST RIDGE, ACROSS 700 FT OF ELEVATION. The row's own instruction is to follow the standard East Ridge glacier track and, at 'roughly 7,500-8,200 ft', leave it and angle up and right beneath a rock band. Research could not narrow that divergence point any further: the two routes share their entire start and only separate when a party traverses climber's-right off the ridge. A 700 ft window on an open glacier is not a marker, and the rock band is not described in a way that distinguishes it from the ground either side of it.
_SKIPPED.wa_south_ridge_4: SUSPECTED PHANTOM, AND THE CATALOG HAS BEEN BURNED BY EXACTLY THIS BEFORE. No Mountain Project page, SummitPost page, CascadeClimbers trip report, AAJ entry or guidebook excerpt describing a distinct South Ridge on Eldorado Peak could be found. The only external mentions are guide-service marketing listing 'the classic East Ridge or South Ridge routes' with no technical content, and those companies' own detailed pages describe only the East Ridge. The row's own content is specific — an obvious crack to a 'U-notch', excellent cracks on the far side, a knife-edge finish — but nothing outside the row corroborates that such a line exists separately from the East Ridge, and this is the same shape as the Forbidden 'East Face / Catscratch' row that was deleted as a phantom. Confirm the route exists before enriching it. See _DEFECTS.

_DEFECTS._note: Data defects noticed in passing while reading these rows. Reported, not fixed — this batch writes only approach_variants.
_DEFECTS.austera_three_rows_one_climb: wa_austera_peak ('Austera Peak', Easy 5th), wa_austera_peak_southwest_ridge ('Southwest Ridge / McAllister Glacier', II 5.2, 3 pitches) and wa_austera_peak_chockstone_route ('Chockstone Route', 3 pitches) all describe the same day: Eldorado camp, Inspiration Glacier, Klawatti Col, the McAllister lobe, the Klawatti-Austera notch at 7,900 ft, a ~75 ft rappel onto the Klawatti Glacier, and a short tower. The Chockstone Route is the SW Ridge's own third pitch. Two rows are written here with the same base and the third is skipped; confirm before deleting any of them, since the aspect labels differ (NE vs SW) and only one carries a grade.
_DEFECTS.klawatti_southeast_face_may_be_the_south: No source found describes a route named 'Southeast Face' on Klawatti Peak. What is documented from Klawatti Col is the SOUTH FACE — a bergschrund, a short 4th-to-easy-5th rock step to clear it, then several hundred feet of 40-55 degree snow — which is exactly what wa_klawatti_peak_southeast_face's own columns describe. A separately named Southeast RIDGE also appears in one search summary. The row's `aspect` is already 'S' while its name says southeast, so the row disagrees with itself.
_DEFECTS.klawatti_two_routes_claim_the_same_first: wa_klawatti_peak_sw_buttress and wa_klawatti_peak_southeast_face both carry `fa` = 'Lloyd Anderson, Karl Boyer, Tom Gorton — July 7, 1940', which is the PEAK's first ascent. The same party and month is also on wa_northwest_ridge (Dorado Needle, July 1940). At most one of the two Klawatti routes can be the 1940 line; the other has inherited the peak's FA rather than its own.
_DEFECTS.goode_northeast_face_beta_looks_borrowed: wa_goode_mountain_northeast_face has season 'Apr-May (spring snow/ice conditions)' and an FA of Beckey and Parrott 1954, but its `beta` reads 'Grade IV 5.5 alpine rock with 6-8 pitches of low 5th class climbing... Best climbing season: mid-July for snowmelt conditions' — the Northeast BUTTRESS's grade, character and season. The row contradicts itself and the beta appears to belong to the neighbouring route.
_DEFECTS.buckner_north_face_waypoints_describe_th: wa_buckner_mountain_north_face's approach prose is explicit and correct that it starts at the BOSTON BASIN trailhead, and says in as many words that this is 'a separate, shorter-drive trailhead than the Cascade Pass TH used for the SW route'. Its `approach_logistics.trailhead` says 'Cascade Pass Trailhead' and its waypoint list runs Cascade Pass Trailhead / Cascade Pass / Sahale Glacier Camp / Sahale-Boston col — i.e. the waypoints walk the OTHER approach from the one the prose drives to. Both approaches are real; the row holds one of each.
_DEFECTS.storm_king_trailhead_row_contradicts_its: wa_storm_king_southwest_scramble stores its trailhead as 'Colonial Creek Campground Trailhead' at 48.6855,-121.0925, and its first waypoint carries the same name at an elevation of 4,875 ft while describing SR-20 'at Rainy Pass (milepost ~158)' and a hike south on the Bridge Creek Trail/PCT. Colonial Creek Campground is at roughly 1,200 ft at milepost 130 — a different trailhead in a different drainage. The waypoint's own note already says the stored trailhead 'is a different, unconnected drainage well north of here and is very likely wrong', so the row is arguing with itself in writing.
_DEFECTS.eldorado_summit_height_stated_three_ways: Within wa_main_peak, high_point_ft is 8872 on three rows, 8873 on wa_south_ridge_4, and the approach prose on several of them says 8,868 ft. wa_eldorado_peak_west_arete also carries 8872 while the area's East Ridge row uses 8868. Small, but it means no figure in this area can be quoted without picking one.
_DEFECTS.dorado_needle_east_ridge_waypoint_is_a_r: wa_dorado_needle_east_ridge's first waypoint is named 'Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)' and its note reads 'Existing DB value (48.492611,-121.117611) appears incorrect — does not match the confirmed roadside trailhead used by the other three Dorado Needle routes; recommend correcting to this value'. The waypoint carries no lat/lng of its own, so it is a note about a correction rather than a location, and nothing on the row states what the corrected value should be.
_DEFECTS.goode_northeast_buttress_trailhead_names: wa_mount_goode_northeast_buttress stores approach_logistics.trailhead as 'Bridge Creek Trailhead (Rainy Pass)' at 48.5075,-120.7312 and a waypoint 'Bridge Creek Trailhead' 0.9 km away. Its two sibling rows (wa_goode_mountain_southwest_couloir, wa_goode_mountain_megalodon_ridge) both use 'Rainy Pass PCT North Trailhead' at 48.5181,-120.7331. Three Goode routes, three slightly different start points for the same walk.
_DEFECTS.tepeh_towers_is_filed_on_eldorado_and_it: wa_tepeh_towers is filed under wa_main_peak, the area beneath wa_eldorado_peak, and its own approach paragraph contains the sentence 'IMPORTANT — this route is NOT on Eldorado Peak itself, despite being filed under the same area'. Its summit waypoint sits 1.7 km from the area coordinate and its high_point_ft is 8,113 against Eldorado's 8,872. The same disclaimer sentence appears verbatim on wa_austera_peak and wa_klawatti_peak_sw_buttress, which are filed on their own peaks and do not need it — so the paragraph has been copied across rows and is only true on one of them.
_DEFECTS.primus_south_ridge_row_mixes_two_approac: wa_primus_peak_south_ridge's approach describes the Eldorado ice-cap traverse from Cascade River Road; its `beta` instead describes the Thunder Creek side ('Mountain Project rates the standard line (there called the East Slope) 3rd class... Most parties treat it as a 3-day trip with a high camp above Borealis Lake'); and its `turnaround` warns about re-crossing Thunder Creek and descending Lucky Ridge. Those are opposite sides of the mountain. Its waypoint list carries the Thunder Creek trailhead while its approach_logistics carries a note saying the Eldorado Creek trailhead was the previous value and is 21.5 km away.
_DEFECTS.requested_peaks_absent_from_the_catalog: RIPSAW RIDGE has no Washington row of any kind — the only matches are co_ripsaw_ridge (on co_peak_c) and co_ripsaw_northeast_ridge (on co_arrowhead), both Colorado. THE TRIPLETS likewise has no North Cascades row; the only Washington match is wa_triplets_the, a 13-route crag under Rocks of Sharon in the SPOKANE area, 300 km away and a completely different formation. Neither absence is a contamination event today, but both are exactly the shape one becomes: a Colorado 'Ripsaw Ridge' and a Spokane 'Triplets' are what a name-based lookup would return for a Cascade Pass request.
